entries.note: PMID 19661377 abstract carries the sentence verbatim; untested is right. Model existed from Schmidt 2008 (cAMP/cGMP), but 2009 is the first abstract-quotable striatal-signalling sentence; acceptable.

Abstract verbatim (PMID 27423256). Twelve healthy volunteers, not patients; neither this abstract nor the rhesus paper (10.1002/syn.21896, only 'warrant further clinical occupancy study') states a cross-species comparison; Delnomdedieu 2017 is HV-only too. No published model-vs-patient comparison: untested.

PMID 25525190, epub 2014-12-18, print 2015; abstract verbatim. Pfizer's rodent exposure-response (Schmidt 2008) predates this; JPET full text returned 403 so no quotable 2008 sentence verified. 2015 start stands under rule 2.

PMID 31205187 abstract verbatim. Adjunctive phase 2 in stable, suboptimally responding outpatients, not acute monotherapy; 'predicted to be adequate' does not name the rodent model. Target reached, no efficacy = contra on the draft's reading; same-vs-contra is a rule call (see rule_questions).
PMID 18287214 abstract verbatim; untested correct. Abstract does not itemize CAR/hyperlocomotion/PPI (MeSH: Motor Activity, Reflex Startle); Grauer 2009 abstract does. Model attribution fine.

PMID 31688451 abstract verbatim; risperidone separated, PF-02545920 did not; contra supported. NCT01175135 results first posted 2018-03-20 (CT.gov API verified), so 2018 under a registry-first rule; Macek epub 2018-09-03 hedges. Keep 2019 unless that rule is adopted.

PMID 25525190 abstract verbatim; untested right. First-use year is probably earlier: Grauer 2009 is MeSH-indexed 'Catalepsy' and Schmidt 2008 ran TP-10 catalepsy; both full texts 403 to me, so no quotable sentence. Flagged, not corrected.

PMID 30190165 abstract verbatim; epub 2018-09-03, print 2019. Same abstract calls TAK-063 'safe and well tolerated' yet reports akathisia/dystonia above placebo at a non-efficacious dose; contra defensible but a rule call. Walling dystonia 1/6/0/3 verified; 'EPS again with MK-8189' not verifiable from Mukai 2026 abstract (25% AE discontinuations at 24 mg, EPS not named).

missing: Engagement: if healthy-volunteer PET is accepted as the patient read-out, Delnomdedieu 2017 (10.1016/j.neuropharm.2017.01.016; 45-63% at 20 mg, Emax model, 93.2 ng/mL for 50% occupancy; PMID 28122201) is the Pfizer-side source, but its abstract carries no cross-species comparison either, so it does not rescue 'same' on its own.

Dose: Mukai 2026 (10.1097/JCP.0000000000002152, PMID 41724750) abstract states 16/24 mg were 'predicted to produce up to 80% sustained enzyme occupancy' and both failed vs placebo while risperidone 6 mg separated; this is the cleanest occupancy-target-reached-and-failed statement in the class and belongs as a 2026 dose entry or as the cited support for the draft's '~80%' claim. The '>50% animal-model threshold' in the judgement is not in the abstract.

Safety: NCT01175135 (registered 2010) pre-specified 'Proportion of Participants With Dystonia Adverse Events' as a PRIMARY outcome and posted results 2018-03-20, so the EPS discordance with the rat screen is datable to 2018 from the registry, a year before Macek/Walling print.

Cell start years: rat catalepsy was run on this class by 2008-2009 (Schmidt 2008 TP-10; Grauer 2009 MeSH 'Catalepsy') and rodent exposure-response for TP-10 is in Schmidt 2008; both JPET full texts returned 403 to WebFetch, so a quote could not be lifted. If rule 6 outranks rule 2, dose and safety should start 2008/2009, not 2015.
rule_questions: Engagement: do healthy-volunteer PET subjects count as 'patients', and does a human PET paper that never cites the primate/rodent prediction count as a 'published comparison'? If both yes, engagement 'same' 2016 stands; if either no, it is untested (my verdict).

Dose: when the rodent-derived exposure/occupancy target is reached in patients and efficacy fails, is that 'same' (exposure translated as predicted) or 'contra' (the target itself was wrong)? The brief's table does not decide; the draft chose contra and I left it.

Registry-first dating: NCT01175135 results (posted 2018-03-20) are a primary source under rule 1 but offer no quotable sentence under rule 2. Which rule sets the year for efficacy and safety contra (2018 vs 2019)?

First-use year (rule 6) vs quotability (rule 2): when the earliest use of a model is only in a paywalled full text with no abstract sentence, does the cell start at the earliest use (2008/2009) or at the first quotable use (2015)?

Safety: can a source whose own summary is 'safe and well tolerated' anchor a 'contra' on a reported EPS excess, and is a weak rat catalepsy signal a correct prediction of EPS ('same') or a wrong prediction of a tolerability window ('contra')?
Year convention: epub vs print (Macek epub 2018-09-03, print 2019; Suzuki epub 2014-12-18, print 2015). The draft uses print throughout; fine if applied consistently across the atlas.
